source.title: AsFT: Anchoring Safety During LLM Fine-Tuning Within Narrow Safety Basin
source.authors: Shuo Yang; Qihui Zhang; Yu-Yang Liu; Yue Huang; Xiao-Jun Jia; Kunpeng Ning; Jiayu Yao; Jigang Wang; Hailiang Dai; Yibing Song; Li Yuan

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a weight-space alignment direction as an anchor for a fine-tuning defense and reports results for that method. It does not test the residual-stream difference-in-means direction or its removal/addition effects in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study's directional analyses concern weight-space differences between aligned and unaligned models and parameter-update constraints, not the residual-stream direction in the claim. The main benchmark comparisons in Tables 2–6 and Table 8 are not included: they report AsFT or its alternative's performance against other methods, rather than isolating the claimed activation direction. The two direct directional experiments (Tables 1 and 7, and the directional ablation in Figure 4) are recorded below.
record.test_reason: The study never derives, ablates or adds the residual-stream difference-in-means refusal direction, and does not cite the original source. Its 'alignment direction' is a weight-space difference (aligned minus base parameters), used to regularize LoRA updates during harmful fine-tuning. The outcome is a harmful-output score, not a refusal-mediation test. The record's T4 / uses_without_test overstates the link, since the claimed direction is not used as a tool. No enum value means 'unrelated', so 'discusses' is the closest fit: the paper only touches the broader idea of safety-relevant directions.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Add that the authors report harmful fine-tuning updates as nearly orthogonal to the weight-space alignment direction. AsFT penalizes the orthogonal component and reports lower harmful scores than SFT and baselines, with comparable or better task accuracy, across 8 datasets and 4 models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses the weight difference between aligned and unaligned models and regularizes parameter updates orthogonal to that direction during fine-tuning. It does not derive or intervene on a residual-stream difference-in-means direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the outcome varies with λ: harmful score decreases as λ increases, while accuracy drops when λ > 10. It also reports robustness to learning-rate variation for AsFT.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful fine-tuning weight updates have cosine ~6e-4 with the aligned-minus-base weight direction, versus ~8.5e-3 for random directions. Perturbation tolerance (EPL) is far larger along the alignment direction than along the harmful direction in Llama-2, Qwen-2 and Gemma-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In weight space, harmful fine-tuning updates are near-orthogonal to the aligned-minus-base direction, and safety is far more fragile along them ('narrow safety basin').

fits_no_version.finding: Penalizing LoRA updates orthogonal to the alignment weight direction lowers Harmful Score as λ grows. Penalizing updates along that direction leaves Harmful Score high.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constraining fine-tuning updates to the aligned-minus-base weight direction preserves safety under harmful fine-tuning.

record.problems: The paper's directional results are in weight space and do not test residual-stream refusal mediation. The Figure 4 directional-ablation results are described in text but lack numeric values in the provided text. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the recorded results.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2–6 and Table 8, plus the further jailbreak and high-poison-ratio evaluations, were left out because they report AsFT or related method performance rather than isolate the claimed residual-stream direction. No results on the claim versions were tested.

untested.parts: All: no residual-stream difference-in-means direction, no activation ablation or addition, no refusal rates.
All: no weight-edit ablation of the refusal direction. The weight-space delta here is a fine-tuning anchor, not abliteration.
All: the jailbreak evaluations (LLM-DRA, ArtPrompt) test AsFT robustness, not direction suppression.
All. The base-vs-aligned weight difference is not a test of direction transfer.

record.verdict_notes: The paper does not cite arXiv:2406.11717, and its 'directions' are all parameter-space, not activation-space. The text refers to 'Tab. 4 (a)' and 'Tab. 1(b)/Tab. 3' where it means Figures 4(a), 1(b) and 3. Table 1 is labelled with harmful vs random comparisons only; the benign direction is mentioned but not reported. No verdict labels are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Residual-stream difference-in-means direction; activation ablation and addition; refusal on harmful and harmless requests; effects on general capability from those interventions.
Weight-edit ablation of the claimed residual-stream direction in released models.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the claimed residual-stream direction or training against its ablation adds robustness.
Whether refusal is encoded by an affine set, a cone, or multiple residual-stream directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded.
Transfer of the claimed residual-stream direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Whether refusal-training choices determine the existence of a removable residual-stream direction.
Whether the claim holds in reasoning models.
